title: APAC Ecosystem Integration Sync - Marketplace & RA
summary: Working sync between Redwood and BlueHarbor to align on APAC marketplace listing, joint reference architecture, listing artifacts, and POC scope. Main blockers: packaging model artifacts for Marketplace registry, VPC connector pattern for private customers, and metering/billing integration. Agreed next steps: share Marketplace checklist, an initial RA diagram, run a small pilot for VPC connector, and schedule a security deep-dive next week.
topics: Reference architecture for private deployments (VPC + connector)
Artifact packaging (OCI vs S3), container images and Helm charts
Billing & metering alignment for marketplace SaaS offers
Security/compliance touchpoints: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs
next_steps: Redwood to share APAC marketplace checklist and a sample listing blob (Lena) - by 2025-08-12
SE to produce initial reference architecture diagram (Samir) - by 2025-08-11
BlueHarbor to provide sample customer network topology for VPC connector testing (Daniel) - by 2025-08-14
Schedule security deep-dive with RedTeam & BlueHarbor security (tentative 2025-08-13)
Create pilot project and invite stakeholders to pilot workspace (Morgan/Lena) - by 2025-08-15
action_items: Lena Ortiz: Send marketplace asset checklist + sample listing manifest (due 2025-08-12)
Samir Gupta: Draft reference architecture diagram + Terraform module pointers (due 2025-08-11)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-07 11:30 JST (03:30Z)
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Morgan (Redwood Partner Ops); Aiko, Daniel, Priya, Kei (BlueHarbor)

Summary: Quick sync to land the technical pieces for a co-listed offering in APAC marketplaces. Focus on RA for private customers and artifacts for marketplace listing. Some audio dropouts early, transcription picks up mid-sentence.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i know we compressed the window a bit for APAC hours so appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:08] Aiko Tanaka: Aiko here from BlueHarbor, hi all.
[00:10] Daniel Park: Daniel, platform.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Priya, solutions.
[00:14] Kei Nakamura: Kei, PM for marketplace stuff.
[00:16] Samir Gupta: Samir here, se at Redwood.
[00:18] Morgan Li: Morgan, partner ops.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: great, thanks. Objective today — line up the technical integration for the marketplace listing and the reference arch for customers who want private deployments. we also want to agree pilot scope.

[00:35] Kei Nakamura: quick context — BlueHarbor has a bunch of enterprise customers in Japan and APAC asking for an on-prem or VPC-private option when they buy ML features. for marketplace listing we need the SaaS offer but also a reference architecture customers can follow. timeline target: get a draft listing ready in the next three weeks.

[00:55] Lena Ortiz: makes sense. on Redwood's side, we have two patterns: hosted API (fast path) and private connector (VPC peering or private link) + private deployment (customer-managed infra) for regulated customers. se, do you want to run through constraints?

[01:10] Samir Gupta: yep. main technical points: 1) packaging model artifacts — marketplace often wants a bundle/manifest; we typically support OCI image push for runtime and an S3-based model bundle for weights, or parity with OCI if you want everything in registry. 2) network path — options are direct peering, private link, or a connector agent in customer's VPC. 3) auth and metering — marketplace metering needs server-side usage logs or a metering hook; Redwood can emit metering events but need agreement on how marketplace will aggregate them.

[01:40] Daniel Park: for us the connector agent is preferable — less peering fuss and we can control egress. question: does Redwood's connector require inbound rule changes?

[01:48] Samir Gupta: short answer, depends on pattern. the agent mode initiates outbound connections to Redwood endpoints, so typically only outbound rules are required, which is good for locked-down customers. the peering/private link options will need infra changes.

[02:05] Priya Menon: on packaging, OCI images make sense for the runtime, but customers want to avoid large images with weights. can we support a split artifact — small runtime image that pulls weights from a customer S3 or from Redwood-hosted object store?

[02:18] Samir Gupta: yes, we do that already — the runtime image is <500MB, weights are stored in an object store and referenced by stable URIs. for marketplace listing we need to be explicit about where weights live and licensing; if BlueHarbor wants to host weights, we'll need a secure S3 presigned workflow or role-based access.

[02:40] Aiko Tanaka: sounds ok. regulatory customers will insist all data and weights stay in region and be encrypted with our KMS. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys?

[02:49] Samir Gupta: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations in the private deployment pattern. for the hosted API we have envelope encryption but cannot integrate with a customer's KMS unless on Dedicated or Private plan.

[03:05] Lena Ortiz: to tie to marketplace listing, we should document which deployment modes are supported per SKU — e.g., SaaS-only SKU vs SaaS+Connector SKU vs Private Deployment SKU. Kei, is that aligned with marketplace requirements?

[03:16] Kei Nakamura: marketplaces prefer clear SKUs. also need: pricing metadata, a support contact, deployment instructions, and tech review. AWS has a security review step that can take 7–10 business days.

[03:30] Daniel Park: the tech review will want diagrams. Samir, can you share a reference architecture diagram that shows data flow, network controls, and where the KMS keys live?

[03:38] Samir Gupta: yes, we'll produce an RA diagram. i'll include Terraform snippets for the connector and a sample helm chart for on-prem.

[03:50] Priya Menon: for pilot success criteria — we want latency under 350ms p95 for chat workloads and cost per 1k tokens under threshold X, and log forwarding to our Splunk instance. can Redwood forward audit logs?

[04:05] Samir Gupta: yes, we support log forwarding via secure syslog/HTTPS endpoints and can stream audit logs and token-level usage. small caveat: streaming detailed KV cache diagnostics is off by default due to PII.

[04:20] Aiko Tanaka: about metering — marketplace needs a usage report that ties to SKU. if Redwood emits token usage events, can you map them to the marketplace line item id?

[04:30] Lena Ortiz: we can. we'll need to instrument the call path to attach a marketplace SKU header or parameter so downstream logs are tagged. Samir, that's feasible?

[04:37] Samir Gupta: yes, we can accept an "X-Marketplace-SKU" header and attach it to billing events. we should validate the header and provide a fallback mapping in case the header is missing.

[04:50] Kei Nakamura: what about container registry compliance — some marketplaces require ECR/Artifact Registry usage. can Redwood push images to the partner's registry?

[04:58] Samir Gupta: we can provide image manifests and a documented push flow; for automation we can run a CI job to push to ECR as part of release. that will require IAM keys on BlueHarbor side or a cross-account role.

[05:12] Daniel Park: question on billing latency — marketplace reconciliation often lags. we need a daily usage file export. does Redwood provide daily usage exports and an S3 drop?

[05:21] Samir Gupta: yes, daily exports to an S3 bucket are supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted API we'll need to enable export and discuss retention. format is CSV/JSON with per-request token counts and timestamps.

[05:34] Lena Ortiz: ok, sounds like blockers are mostly paperwork and infra details. let's talk about security review items: SOC 2 artifacts, pen test reports, and encryption controls. BlueHarbor, what do you need to sign off?

[05:45] Aiko Tanaka: our security team will require SOC 2 type II, recent pen test summary, and a data flow with encryption callouts. also compliance for APAC data residency.

[05:55] Samir Gupta: we can share SOC 2 and a redacted penetration test summary; for private deployments we can give more detailed artifacts under an NDA.

[06:05] Kei Nakamura: another practical item — listing screenshots and a 2-minute walk-through video of onboarding. can Redwood provide a short demo clip?

[06:12] Morgan Li: yes, partner ops can record a 3-step onboarding video and provide screen captures of the console flows. we'll put that in a partner artifacts folder.

[06:22] Priya Menon: about the RA — include both public SaaS flow for low friction customers and the connector/agent flow for locked-down customers; maybe a hybrid where weights are mirrored to a regional object store.

[06:35] Samir Gupta: good point — i'll add a mirror pattern: weights in partner-controlled regional S3 with replication and a signed access model for runtime pulls.

[06:46] Aiko Tanaka: for the pilot, can BlueHarbor spin up one existing customer to act as pilot? we want to test onboarding and billing mapping.

[06:55] Daniel Park: yes, we have a customer in Tokyo that is comfortable being a pilot. they have a VPC and Splunk logging. we can provision test accounts next week.

[07:05] Lena Ortiz: perfect. next, a couple of nitty-gritty technical questions from my side — what's the KV cache behavior across connector mode? will it remain on Redwood side or do connectors cache locally?

[07:18] Samir Gupta: KV cache stays on the serving runtime; connector only proxies requests. we do support a local edge cache for prefix caching in rare cases but that's optional and requires a small footprint.

[07:30] Priya Menon: about upgrades — customers worry about breaking changes on model rollouts. does Redwood support pinned model versions with canary traffic?

[07:37] Samir Gupta: yes, the platform supports pinning versions per-customer, canaries, A/B rollouts, and automatic fallback to a previous model if regressions are detected. we'll detail rollout policies in the RA.

[07:50] Kei Nakamura: marketplace also wants to know about support SLAs and where tickets go. do we provide a joint support path?

[07:58] Lena Ortiz: typical pattern is partner handles first-line and Redwood provides a dedicated channel for escalations; for enterprise customers we can set up a shared escalation runbook. Morgan will own the runbook.

[08:10] Morgan Li: yes, i'll create a runbook template and share with Kei.

[08:20] Aiko Tanaka: ok what about data residency for logs? some customers want logs stored only in-region and not replicated.

[08:28] Samir Gupta: we can limit log replication and set retention at the account level for Dedicated/Private. hosted customers have region selection and retention controls, but some logs (control plane) may be centralized. we'll call that out explicitly in the RA.

[08:45] Daniel Park: technical deep dive question — performance profiling. do you have benchmarks for p95 latency for model X on a single instance? we want baseline numbers to present to customers.

[08:55] Samir Gupta: we do. i'll attach a perf profile for the model family we'll list. note that p95 varies with sequence length and batching. for small chat seq lengths (~256 tokens) p95 is ~120ms on our optimized runtime given the dedicated GPU config; on smaller instances it will be higher. we'll include a matrix.

[09:12] Priya Menon: perfect. also, is the connector agent supported on RHEL8? some of our customers are strict on OS.

[09:18] Samir Gupta: agent supports RHEL8 and Ubuntu LTS, with a small glibc footprint. we'll produce an install matrix.

[09:28] Lena Ortiz: sounds like we have the technical checklist. before we wrap, any open concerns or blockers?

[09:35] Kei Nakamura: timeline — need confirmation on who publishes the listing and who submits security artifacts. Kei will publish but needs Redwood assets by Aug 12 to hit our internal window.

[09:45] Lena Ortiz: agreed. we'll meet those dates. one last ask: can Redwood provide a short legal blurb for the marketplace terms that we can paste into the listing regarding data handling?

[09:54] Morgan Li: yes, partner ops will coordinate with legal and share a short blurb.

[10:05] Lena Ortiz: OK great. let's recap next steps quickly. Samir will create RA and terraform snippets, Lena will send checklist, Morgan will record onboarding video, BlueHarbor will share topology and confirm pilot customer. security deep-dive scheduled next week.

[10:28] Daniel Park: one micro note, can we get a sandbox account with 10k free token quota for pilot testing?
[10:33] Lena Ortiz: yes we can create a pilot workspace with credits; Morgan will set that up and invite the pilot customer.

[10:40] Priya Menon: thanks everyone, that was useful.
[10:42] Aiko Tanaka: thanks, bye.
[10:44] Samir Gupta: thanks all.

Meeting end.

References & artifacts mentioned:
- Marketplace checklist (to be shared)
- Reference architecture diagram + Terraform snippets (to be shared)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional dropouts and speaker labels sometimes simplified; some technical terms transcribed phonetically (e.g., "ECR" as "E-C-R"), and timestamps are approximate.
